newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HONGKONG TO BAN OVERHEIGHT VESSELS NEAR NEW AIRPORT.
newsitem.headline: HONGKONG TO BAN OVERHEIGHT VESSELS NEAR NEW AIRPORT.

text.p: The Hong Kong government said on Wednesday it plans to ban overheight vessels from waters around bridges leading to the territory's new airport.

The Shipping and Port Control (Amendment) Regulation 1997 will also ensure tall vessels do not obstruct the flight path or air navigation signals near Chek Lap Kok airport, which is due to open next April.

In a statement, the government said it needs to control the movement of vessels in the Chek Lap Kok Airport Approach Areas and make sure no overheight vessels attempt to pass under the Tung Chung, Kap Shui Mun or Tsing Ma bridges.
The statement did not specify the height of vessels which will be restricted. A Marine Department spokesman was not available for comment.
The new bridges form the Lantau Link that connects the new airport to the Kowloon peninsula.

The air cargo industry recently voiced its concern about the potential disaster of a ship crashing into one of the bridges. It is feared that if the bridge link were ever cut, the airport would be paralysed and Hong Kong's economy immediately affected.
A barge derrick is reported to have crashed into the Kap Shui Mun bridge last year, raising safety concerns and the need for vessels to be regulated, industry observers said.
The government is also set to repeal restrictions on vessels entering prohibited waters near Hong Kong's existing Kai Tak airport when it is replaced by Chek Lap Kok.
